newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia PM sees rejection of job dismissal plan.
newsitem.headline: Australia PM sees rejection of job dismissal plan.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday he expected the government's move to exempt small businesses from unfair dismissal laws to be blocked in the upper house of parliament, the senate.
The Opposition said on Tuesday it would oppose the plan to allow businesses with up to 15 employees to dismiss staff within the first year if their work was unsatisfactory.
"... If, as I fear, the Democrats and (independent) Senator (Brian) Harradine support the Labor Party then that regulation will be disallowed," Howard told Melbourne radio 3AW.

"That will disappoint the job hopes of many people and it will also anger, quite rightly, the small business community of Australia, who see the unfair dismissal law in its present form as a major barrier to job generation."
Opposition leader Kim Beazley said on Tuesday Labor would oppose the proposal on the grounds that it ignored employees who had a legitimate claim for unfair dismissal.
Between them, the opposition, the Australian Democrats, the Greens minor party and either of the two independent senators can block government legislation in the Senate.
The exemption was due to take effect from July 1.
